content_html:
Synchronicity Field‑Notes Template

Bias Checks + Mutual‑Information Cheat‑Sheet

A template designed for quick event capture + bias mitigation; suitable for printing to A4 or pasting into your notes. Save one copy per event.

How to Use

  1. Name your narrative state (what you’re currently primed to notice).
  2. Log the external event and identify the minimal overlapping structure.
  3. Run bias checks and a quick base‑rate estimate.
  4. Compute a pragmatic score (how actionable this meaning is).
  5. Close the loop: take one small action and observe the outcome in 24–72 hours.

1) Narrative State

What am I currently seeking/concerned with?

  • Aim: ____________________________
  • Emotional tone (−2…+2): _____
  • Active priors/keywords (3): ____, ____, ____

2) Event Log

  • Date/Time: ________________________
  • Place/Context: _____________________
  • Event (bare description): ____________
  • Minimal overlap with Narrative State: ___

3) Bias & Null Checks

Check Question Pass?
Confirmation Would this feel as meaningful if my current aim were different? [ ]
Selection Did I also notice similar events that I
didn’t
log?		 [ ]
Base rate How often does this kind of event happen weekly? [ ]
Multiple comparisons How many features could have matched by chance? [ ]
Emotion tag Is salience mainly affective (arousal/valence)? [ ]

Null sampling reminder: Log a random 30‑minute “null window” this week to estimate background coincidence rate.

4) Quick Base‑Rate Estimator

Rough probability of overlap this week:

Independent event frequency (per week) ____
Features that could match (N) ____
Matched features (k) ____
Heuristic overlap p ≈ (k/N) × frequency ____

If p is not obviously tiny (≪1%), treat the meaning as plausible but ordinary until reinforced by outcomes.

5) Mutual‑Information Mini Cheat‑Sheet

Two variables X (inner model) and Y (event) share information if knowing one reduces uncertainty about the other. A practical proxy:

  • Specificity: How narrowly defined was my prior? (low entropy)
  • Simplicity: Is the overlap explainable by few features? (short code length)
  • Stability: Does the overlap repeat across contexts/time?

Heuristic MI score (0–6): Specificity (0–2) + Simplicity (0–2) + Stability (0–2) = ____ / 6

6) Pragmatic Action Score

Dimension 0 1 2
Actionability Vague Small step Clear next step
Risk High Moderate Low
Reversibility Hard Partial Easy
Learning value Low Some High

Pragmatic Score (0–8): ______

Decision: [ ] Ignore [ ] Note only [ ] Take minimal reversible action

7) Close the Loop

  • Planned micro‑action (24–72h): _____________________________
  • Outcome observed: ________________________________________
  • Update priors (what changed?): ______________________________
